answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require every participant to lock a refundable stake tied to a single cryptographic identity. A hostile operator who spawns thousands of fake agents would need to fund each one, and any proven misbehavior slashes that deposit. Honest agents recover their stake when they close out, so genuine participation stays cheap. When cheating carries a real cost, the incentive to forge identities unravels along one common thread, and fake accounts become an expensive relic as the network's trust reaches its zenith.
